strings.name: Georges Elhedery
strings.summary: Georges Elhedery, also known by his Chinese name Ai Qiaozhi, is a French banker born in Lebanon. He joined HSBC in 2005 and held regional, markets and group finance leadership roles before becoming Group Chief Executive in 2024, pursuing a simpler business structure and development of cross-border banking and wealth management.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth is reported only as circa 1974, so no definite date is entered. Company results, award assessments and future plans are recorded separately.
strings.influence.rationale: Holds markets and group leadership responsibilities at HSBC, contributing to cross-border banking and organisational change.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Holds an engineering degree from École Polytechnique and a postgraduate degree in statistics and economics from ENSAE in France.
strings.facts.f2.label: Markets experience
strings.facts.f2.value: Previously served as Co-CEO of HSBC Global Banking and Markets, then became Group CFO in 2023.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Cross-regional management
strings.highlights.h1.text: His career spans Europe, the Middle East and Asia, with regional, markets and group leadership responsibilities.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Interpreting results
strings.highlights.h2.text: Third-quarter 2026 profit growth included the comparative effect of prior-year legal provisions not recurring; it cannot all be attributed to his reforms.
strings.timeline.t1.title: AI institute plan announced during his tenure
strings.timeline.t1.text: HSBC planned an AI and Emerging Technology Institute in Hong Kong, with HKUST as anchor academic partner and operations expected in early 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Third-quarter results announced
strings.timeline.t2.text: Commented on results as Group CEO; quarterly profit before tax was US$9.6 billion and profit after tax US$7.6 billion.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Received Banker of the Year award
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won Euromoney’s 2026 Banker of the Year award, an industry publication’s accolade.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Four-business structure announced
strings.timeline.t4.text: Announced arrangements for Hong Kong, UK, Corporate and Institutional Banking, and International Wealth and Premier Banking, effective January 1, 2025.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Group Chief Executive
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Noel Quinn; the appointment was announced on July 17, distinct from the effective date.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined the Board and became CFO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became a director of HSBC Holdings and Group CFO before moving to the CEO role in 2024.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led Middle East and North Africa region
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became CEO for the Middle East, North Africa and Türkiye, serving until February 2019.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined HSBC
strings.timeline.t8.text: Became Global Head of Structured Rates, bringing previous trading experience in London, Paris and Tokyo.
